answer: Modern phones combine several frequency bands at once, and the combination available depends on the serving tower and the handset's position, a signature written by the network itself, bright as saffron in sunlight. The verifier checks that the reported band combination is one the tower actually offers, and a plume of smoke cannot hide a wrong band, since an antenna cannot receive a frequency the tower never transmits. An oasis of clones fails together when they all claim the same rare combination, while genuine users show the varied combinations of a real city.
